$comment: The canonical capability registry required by the operator's Sovereign Execution Standard (Phase 1, §5). Hand-authored fields only: what a person must state (name, symbol, contract, dependencies, security requirements, limitations, known risks, economic relevance). evidence_level, lifecycle_state, tests and integration are ALL derived by scripts/capability_map.py from what actually resolves and is actually referenced -- never typed here, for the same reason nodes.json's 'verified' is the one field a machine may not set. This is a first, deliberately small cut: 8 capabilities chosen because their evidence is unambiguous, not an attempt at completeness. Scope: engine/ (Python) only -- the TypeScript root app's own capabilities (credit ledger, module registry, budget/metering) are a known gap of this first version, stated rather than silently omitted.

capabilities.name: Money as exact pico-dollar integers
capabilities.description: All currency is an int in 1e-12 USD, never a float, so a router that saves a fraction of a cent on a cheap-model call reports the saving instead of rounding it to zero.
capabilities.contract: Every arithmetic operation on Money returns Money; there is no float currency path anywhere in the package.
capabilities.limitations: Exact only to the pico-dollar; does not model currencies other than USD.
capabilities.known_risks: A future contributor introducing a float intermediate in a new module would silently reintroduce the class of bug this exists to prevent -- money_is_int_picos in invariants.json is the structural guard against that.
capabilities.economic_relevance: Every priced call in the engine (router, MCP tools, factory economics) is denominated in this type; a defect here corrupts every cost figure the platform reports.

capabilities.name: Injected clock
capabilities.description: Nothing in the engine calls datetime.now() or time.monotonic() directly; every time-dependent component takes a Clock, so a FakeClock can advance an hour-long TTL in a test that runs in milliseconds.
capabilities.contract: A Clock exposes now() and monotonic(); FakeClock and SystemClock are interchangeable everywhere one is accepted.
capabilities.limitations: Two files are allowlisted exceptions to direct time access, each naming the parameter that already provides injection -- see invariants.json's time_is_injected entry.
capabilities.known_risks: A new module calling time.monotonic() directly would make its behaviour untestable without real wall-clock waits, and would not be caught except by invariant_map.py's checker.
capabilities.economic_relevance: None directly; this is why the 1,200+ test suite runs in seconds rather than hours.

capabilities.name: Cost-aware model routing
capabilities.description: Routes a request cheap-first, verifies the cheap answer, escalates only on failure -- measured at 42.4% of always-strong spend at equal accuracy against a capability-modelled benchmark.
capabilities.contract: Router.route() returns a RoutedCompletion carrying which tier actually answered and what the same request would have cost on the reference tier.
security_requirements: A verifier must not itself be escalated past what the routing policy allows.
capabilities.limitations: The 42.4% figure is measured against omnex.llm.fakes.CapabilityModel, a deterministic stand-in whose capability-is-monotone-in-tier assumption does not capture every real-provider failure mode.
capabilities.known_risks: A verifier that is too lenient makes the router look cheaper than it is by accepting wrong cheap answers; break_even() is three-valued specifically so an under-measured verifier reads UNKNOWN rather than a false PASS.
capabilities.economic_relevance: Directly: this is the single largest per-call cost lever the platform has.

capabilities.name: RAG citation grounding
capabilities.description: Checks each claim in a generated answer against the retrieved evidence and reports a support rate, at 25-30k sentences/sec flat with document size.
capabilities.contract: Grounder.check(answer, evidence) returns which claims are supported and which are dropped, never a single aggregate score.
security_requirements: Citations are stripped before number extraction so a URL's date is never misread as an asserted figure.
capabilities.limitations: A stated, deliberately-preserved limitation: a paraphrase outside the corpus is missed (test_a_paraphrase_outside_the_corpus_is_missed is meant to stay green).
capabilities.known_risks: The sentence splitter exists twice (here and in citegate) and has diverged before; twin_splitters_agree in invariants.json is the guard.
capabilities.economic_relevance: Indirect: grounding failures are the most expensive kind of quality failure for a content-generation product to ship silently.

capabilities.name: Injection fence
capabilities.description: Detects prompt-injection attempts in untrusted content before it reaches a model, measured at 30/30 known attack patterns caught with 1/30 false positives.
capabilities.contract: Every tool result and retrieved chunk is tagged with a Provenance and only UNTRUSTED content passes through the detector before a prompt is assembled.
security_requirements: A ToolResult can never be constructed with a trusted Provenance -- structural, not conventional (__post_init__ refuses it).
capabilities.limitations: 30 attack patterns is a fixed, committed benchmark corpus, not an exhaustive adversarial test; a genuinely novel injection technique is untested by construction.
capabilities.known_risks: The one false positive in the 30/30 benchmark is a known, accepted trade-off, not an unmeasured gap.
capabilities.economic_relevance: None directly measured; a bypassed fence is a security incident, not a cost line.

capabilities.name: MCP per-tool permission scoping
capabilities.description: A registered tool can require a named permission; an unauthorized tools/call is refused with the identical error and payload shape as calling a nonexistent tool, so a caller without a permission cannot learn the tool exists.
capabilities.contract: McpServer.available_to(granted) filters both tools/list and tools/call identically; granted=None stays fully unrestricted so no caller loses a tool it never opted into losing.
security_requirements: An out-of-scope tool call must never return a distinguishable error from a nonexistent one.
required_permission is never read from or written to the wire.
capabilities.limitations: Permissions are a flat frozenset[str], not a role hierarchy or wildcard system -- deliberate, since nothing in this codebase yet has more than one caller identity.
capabilities.known_risks: A future caller-identity system with roles would need to flatten roles to a permission set before calling available_to(), and a buggy flattening could over- or under-grant.
capabilities.economic_relevance: None directly; this is an access-control capability, not a priced one.

capabilities.name: Hybrid dense/lexical retrieval
capabilities.description: Combines dense vector similarity and lexical (BM25-style) search via reciprocal rank fusion, rather than relying on either alone.
capabilities.contract: HybridStore.search() returns SearchHit objects ranked by fused score, never raw cosine similarity alone.
capabilities.limitations: The qdrant-backed adapter is a partial extra (1 of 3 declared dependencies imported); the in-process store is what every test exercises.
capabilities.known_risks: A cross-embedding-space comparison (mixing chunks embedded by two different models) would produce a meaningless cosine score; guarded explicitly in fusion.py per its own docstring.
capabilities.economic_relevance: Indirect: retrieval quality is the ceiling on CAP-004's grounding rate.

capabilities.name: Eval regression gate
capabilities.description: Blocks a deploy on any case that passed and now fails, never on the mean -- because a flat aggregate hides five regressions behind five simultaneous improvements.
capabilities.contract: Gate.decide() compares a run to its baseline case-by-case and refuses to compare across a changed suite fingerprint.
capabilities.limitations: The default metrics are deterministic and in-process; judge_quality() in judge.py is a separate, non-gating metric by design (variance between runs would make a noisy gate teach a team to disable it).
capabilities.known_risks: Editing an expected answer and re-running looks identical to a real improvement unless the suite fingerprint is checked first -- which is why a fingerprint mismatch raises rather than silently comparing.
capabilities.economic_relevance: Indirect: this is what stands between a bad model swap and a live regression a customer sees.
